overview.short: High-altitude desert, ancient Key Monastery, Chandratal Lake and star-filled skies.
overview.description: Spiti Valley is a cold desert mountain valley in north-eastern Himachal Pradesh at 3,800m. Its stark, treeless landscapes, ancient Buddhist monasteries, and villages accessible only in summer months make it one of India's most remote and extraordinary destinations.

routes.byAir: Fly to Kullu (KUU) then 6–7 hr drive
routes.via:
Route 1: Delhi→Shimla→Narkanda→Reckong Peo→Kaza (2 days)
Route 2: Delhi→Manali→Rohtang→Kunzum→Kaza (1 day from Manali)

howToReach.roadNote: Only accessible Jun–Sep. The Manali–Spiti route is considered one of the greatest road trips in the world. 4WD strongly recommended.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit Spiti Valley?
faq.a: The best time to visit Spiti Valley is Jun – Sep. Summers are 5–25°C and winters are -30 to -10°C.

faq.q: How do I reach Spiti Valley?
faq.a: The nearest airport is Bhuntar Airport, Kullu (KUU) (245 km) and the nearest railway station is Shimla Railway Station (narrow gauge) (230 km). Only accessible Jun–Sep. The Manali–Spiti route is considered one of the greatest road trips in the world. 4WD strongly recommended.

faq.q: How many days are enough for Spiti Valley?
faq.a: 4 days are usually enough to cover the top attractions of Spiti Valley at a relaxed pace.

faq.q: How much does a hotel cost in Spiti Valley?
faq.a: Stays in Spiti Valley start from ₹700 per night, with options across 6 price categories.

faq.q: What are the top places to visit in Spiti Valley?
faq.a: The top attractions are Key Monastery (Ki Gompa), Chandratal Lake, Hikkim Post Office, Dhankar Monastery & Lake, Pin Valley National Park.
